clue.text: Literary London bird's performing — the name can be quickly given

definitions.text: the name can be quickly given

parts.note: Jack London was the American author of The Call of the Wild, so the literary London gives his first name
the robin is a bird; the possessive supplies the S
a show that is on is being performed

explanation.surface: A London novelist's bird puts on a show, and its name can be rattled off fast.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the idiom 'before you can say ...', used of something done very quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the name in the idiom 'before you can say it', meaning in an instant, so it is a name said quickly.

clue.text: Flower for Scottish sweetheart — nothing out of the question in short

parts.note: jo is a Scots word for a sweetheart, as in Burns's 'John Anderson, my jo'

indicators.note: nothing lies out of, that is outside, the shortened question, so its letters go round it

parts.note: nil means nothing
QU is a short form of question

explanation.surface: A flower given to a Scottish darling, with no doubts at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' puts NIL around QU, giving NQUIL after JO.
explanation.definitionFit: A jonquil is a kind of narcissus with fragrant yellow blooms, a garden flower.

clue.text: Whereby Milton entertained the company with some music

indicators.note: only some of the word music is used, its last two letters dropped

explanation.surface: Milton laid on a party for his guests with a bit of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' trims IC off music to leave MUS. The definition refers to Milton's masque of 1634, a stage entertainment.
explanation.definitionFit: Comus is the masque by John Milton, a courtly entertainment with songs, so it is the work through which the poet entertained.

clue.text: Confound or derange an instrument

indicators.note: to confound is to throw into confusion, so the letters of the next words are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A command to muddle and disorder a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confound' rearranges the nine letters of OR DERANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A reed organ is a keyboard instrument such as a harmonium whose sound comes from vibrating reeds.

clue.text: Blast — or a milder expletive

explanation.surface: An exclamation of annoyance, or a gentler curse instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A blast of wind is a gust that blows; and 'blow it!' is a mild oath, softer than 'blast'.

clue.text: Midweek friend edited The Beacon

indicators.note: an edited text has been reworked, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the middle letters of the word week are its two Es
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mate halfway through the week has edited a newspaper called The Beacon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Midweek' gives EE from the centre of 'week'; 'edited' shuffles EE with FRIEND.
explanation.definitionFit: A need-fire is a bonfire lit as a signal or in old rural rites, so a signal blaze on a hill.

clue.text: Wizard's home, one needing a form of gas

parts.note: the Wizard of Oz lives in the land of Oz
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Wizard's residence and someone in need of a gas supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is an allotrope of oxygen, a gas with three atoms in each molecule.

clue.text: Jokes about the French doctor's celebratory get-up

indicators.note: the jokes word goes about, around, the next pieces

parts.note: gags are jokes
la is French for the (feminine)
DR is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: Jokes about a French physician's party outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad rags is informal for one's best clothes, worn for a party or special occasion.

clue.text: Direction to purify the plant

parts.note: S, south, is a compass direction
to purge is to cleanse or purify

explanation.surface: An instruction telling someone to cleanse the factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Spurge is a plant of the genus Euphorbia, many with milky sap.

clue.text: The egoist's favourite figure

parts.note: a self-centred person's preferred number, and preferred person, is himself

explanation.surface: Which number does a self-obsessed person like best?
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means oneself, the person an egoist puts first, and also the digit 1, a figure.

clue.text: Flower has a neat mouthpiece

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox
a lip is part of the mouth

explanation.surface: A flower with a tidy mouthpiece, like an instrument's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' looks like an adjective meaning tidy, but here it is the old noun for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: The oxlip is a wild primula with pale yellow blooms, related to the cowslip.

clue.text: Skier's final result

explanation.surface: The last outcome for someone on the slopes.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a skier is a ball hit high into the air, a shot upwards; 'Skier's' reads as 'a skier is'. It is not a person skiing.
explanation.definitionFit: A skier is a stroke lofted high, a shot going up; and the outcome or conclusion of events is the upshot.

clue.text: One breaking the rules of the fireguard

parts.note: taken as written
a fender is a low guard in front of a fireplace

explanation.surface: Someone who ignores the regulations governing the fireguard.
explanation.definitionFit: An offender is a person who commits a crime or breaks a law.

clue.text: Where lizards loll

parts.note: a room for relaxing, from the phrase for idle men who hang around bars and hotels

explanation.surface: The place reptiles lie about lazily.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'lounge lizard' is an idle man who frequents fashionable bars looking for rich company; the clue pictures reptiles instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A lounge is a sitting room for relaxation, where idlers called lizards lie about.

clue.text: Lacking the skill and experience of poets?

definitions.text: Lacking the skill and experience of poets?

parts.words: Lacking the skill and experience of poets?
parts.note: having no knowledge, and humorously not written in metrical lines as poets write

explanation.surface: Without the craft or background that poets have.
explanation.definitionFit: Unversed means inexperienced or unskilled in something, and the question mark suggests a lack of poetry.

clue.text: First wife born behind bars — what a game!

indicators.note: to be behind bars is to be imprisoned, so the pieces go inside the barred enclosure

parts.note: a cage is made of bars
Eve, the first wife, was made from Adam's rib

explanation.surface: A man's first wife is born in prison, a dramatic turn of events.
explanation.walkthrough: RIB for 'First wife' leans on Genesis, where Eve is made from Adam's rib.
explanation.definitionFit: Cribbage is a card game scored with pegs on a board.

clue.text: Head of department is put up in superior (if modest) accommodation

indicators.note: the pieces are put in the word for superior

parts.note: better means superior

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
in a down clue, putting a word up reads it from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A head of department is lodged in quite good, if modest, digs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns IS into SI, which follows D inside BETTER. '(if modest)' qualifies the accommodation: a bedsit is a small single room.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed-sitter is a single rented room used for both sleeping and living, a modest lodging.

clue.text: Wrote about many being accused

indicators.note: the word for wrote goes about, around, the letter for many

parts.note: to indite is an old word meaning to write or compose
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many

explanation.surface: Someone wrote about many people facing charges.
explanation.definitionFit: To be indicted is to be formally charged with a crime.

clue.text: The rainbow sign of this undertaking

definitions.text: The rainbow sign of this undertaking

parts.words: The rainbow sign of this undertaking
parts.note: in Genesis, God set the rainbow in the sky as the sign of his promise to Noah never to flood the earth again

explanation.surface: A rainbow signals a solemn promise.
explanation.definitionFit: A covenant is a binding agreement or solemn pledge, like God's promise after the Flood.

clue.text: Sum demanded for service — a heraldic device

explanation.surface: A bill for service, and a coat-of-arms emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge is a fee asked for a service; in heraldry a charge is any figure placed on a shield.

clue.text: Port that has poems written to it

parts.note: odes are lyric poems
it can mean sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: A harbour town that has had verses addressed to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' meaning sex appeal (as in the 'It girl') is a crossword convention for SA.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa is a major port on the Black Sea in Ukraine.

clue.text: Missionary saint in a measure

indicators.note: the saint is placed in the word for measure

parts.note: a pole is an old unit of length, about five metres

explanation.surface: A saint on a missionary journey, within a set distance.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostle is one sent to spread a faith, such as the twelve disciples or early Christian missionaries.

clue.text: Take off here with melody and burlesque entertainment

parts.note: an air is a tune
a strip, striptease, is a staple of burlesque shows

explanation.surface: Get undressed here to music in a cabaret show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' looks like undressing, fitting the burlesque surface, but it means an aircraft leaving the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: An airstrip is a basic runway where aircraft land and take to the air.

clue.text: Capital also lies outside state boundaries

indicators.note: the word for also lies outside the state, wrapping round it

parts.note: too means also
KY is the abbreviation for the US state of Kentucky, which is also its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A capital city also sits beyond the borders of a state.
explanation.walkthrough: KY, Kentucky, is formed by that state's outermost letters, which explains 'boundaries'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tokyo is the capital city of Japan.

clue.text: Pop engagement, see? Nothing in it for a ladies' man

indicators.note: nothing is put in it, the whole formed by the previous pieces

parts.note: a gig is a booking for a pop group
lo is an old word meaning look or see
O, the shape of zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A pop booking, see? There's nothing in it for a womaniser.
explanation.definitionFit: A gigolo is a man paid to escort women, a kept man.

clue.text: Nymph's love study

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O
to read is to study, as in reading law

explanation.surface: A nymph's romantic reading matter.
explanation.definitionFit: An oread is a mountain nymph in Greek mythology.

clue.text: Churchman rode a nag within this forest

indicators.note: the answer lies within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A clergyman rode an old horse through the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this forest' gives a second definition: the Forest of Dean is an ancient forest in Gloucestershire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A dean is a senior cleric heading a cathedral chapter, and the same name belongs to the Forest of Dean.

clue.text: Language incomprehensible

explanation.surface: Speech that can't be understood.
explanation.definitionFit: Greek is the tongue of Greece, and 'it's all Greek to me' means it is unintelligible.

clue.text: What the doctor ordered-matter arranged with Ear, Nose and Throat

indicators.note: arranged letters are set out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
ENT is the hospital department for ear, nose and throat

explanation.surface: A doctor's prescription: the business sorted out with the ENT clinic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' reorders MATTER into TREATM. 'What the doctor ordered' looks like an anagram signal on 'ordered' but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Treatment is the medical care a physician prescribes for a patient.

clue.text: Broken down? Spanner needed

parts.note: a nursery rhyme's line about collapse, with a span over the Thames as the thing that spans

explanation.surface: Has the car broken down? Fetch a spanner.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme begins 'London Bridge is broken down'; a spanner here is something that spans a river, not a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous Thames crossing in the rhyme 'is broken down', and a bridge is a structure that spans.
